issues.spec_citation: CQL 1.5.3 Nullological Operators: IsTrue(null) and IsFalse(null) return false.
issues.evidence: Direct DuckDB probes over typed BOOLEAN NULL returned SQL NULL for IsTrue(NULL::BOOLEAN) and IsFalse(NULL::BOOLEAN), while the official CQL nullological examples expect false.
issues.root_cause: The IsTrue/IsFalse macros compared nullable booleans directly and did not coalesce the comparison result to false.
issues.resolution: Updated logical macros so IsTrue/IsFalse require BOOLEAN input and coalesce nullable comparisons to false.
issues.verification: Nullological parity tests passed on native-loaded and forced Python fallback registrations; official CQL nullological conformance passed.

issues.spec_citation: CQL DateTime(year, month, day) constructs a DateTime with day precision, distinct from a Date.
issues.evidence: Translated DateTime(2000, 1, 1) produced a date-shaped value without the day-precision DateTime marker, which broke historical Coalesce DateTime examples and downstream DateTime interval semantics.
issues.root_cause: The temporal constructor lowered three-component DateTime values to YYYY-MM-DD without preserving DateTime identity.
issues.resolution: Changed DateTime(year, month, day) lowering to emit the explicit day-precision marker YYYY-MM-DDT in literal and runtime paths.
issues.verification: Focused temporal/nullological parity tests passed and official DateTime nullological examples remained at 100% conformance.

issues.spec_citation: CQL Coalesce returns the first non-null argument across supported overloads, including DateTime values.
issues.evidence: Direct public DuckDB Coalesce over TIMESTAMP values failed in the Python fallback path because Python datetime objects were not serialized into a stable return value.
issues.root_cause: The generic Coalesce return helper handled scalar JSON/string values but not Python datetime objects returned by DuckDB for TIMESTAMP inputs.
issues.resolution: Normalized Python datetime return values to ISO strings in the Coalesce helper before returning through DuckDB.
issues.verification: Focused nullological parity tests passed on native-loaded and forced Python fallback registrations.

issues.spec_citation: CQL partial-precision DateTime values must remain parseable and comparable at their declared precision.
issues.evidence: After preserving YYYY-MM-DDT, Python and native C++ date/time helper parsers rejected that marker form in date/time and interval helper paths.
issues.root_cause: The helper parsers accepted year, month, full date, and timestamp shapes but did not recognize the day-precision DateTime marker used internally to distinguish DateTime from Date.
issues.resolution: Added YYYY-MM-DDT parsing support to Python datetime helpers and native C++ datetime parsing.
issues.verification: Native C++ SQL tests, focused day-precision parity tests, and official CQL conformance all passed.

issues.spec_citation: CQL predecessor/successor and interval operations respect point precision for DateTime values.
issues.evidence: Official CQL cases for predecessor/successor of DateTime(2000,1,1) and DateTime interval contains/meets/collapse/except initially regressed after day-precision DateTime identity was restored.
issues.root_cause: Boundary stepping and interval normalization treated day-precision DateTime markers inconsistently across Python and native C++ helpers.
issues.resolution: Made predecessor/successor, interval parsing, normalization, collapse, contains, meets, and output formatting preserve explicit day-precision DateTime markers in both Python and native C++ paths.
issues.verification: Official CQL conformance passed 1706/1706; native C++ SQL suite passed 628 assertions.

issues.spec_citation: CQL interval open-bound normalization must use the actual operand precision, not wall-clock midnight heuristics.
issues.evidence: DQM focused runs exposed CMS165/CMS56 risk: full timestamp open upper bounds at midnight were normalized as day-precision values, excluding late-day events such as 2026-06-30T23:59:59.000+00:00.
issues.root_cause: Python and native interval helpers inferred day precision from midnight timestamps, and dateAddQuantity/dateSubtractQuantity dropped the YYYY-MM-DDT marker for true day-precision DateTime inputs.
issues.resolution: Removed the midnight heuristic for full timestamps, made open-bound stepping raw-value aware, preserved explicit day-precision markers through date arithmetic, and mirrored the behavior in native C++.
issues.verification: Focused DQM CMS165/CMS56 passed 100%; full DQM passed 47/47; full conformance passed 2822/2822; full fhir4ds pytest passed 7157.
